time.timezone_desc: The time zone that decides when a billing month starts and ends.
time.billing_month_hint: Applies right away. At midnight on the 1st in this time zone the billing period closes and a new one starts. Open sessions are not interrupted.
time.billing_timezone_hint: Example: Europe/Warsaw. Affects package monthly usage and overage totals.
time.ntp_desc: Keep the NeoDesk server clock synchronized so billable session times are accurate.
time.custom_timezone_hint: A name like Europe/Berlin or America/New_York. It replaces the choice in the list.

time.require_sync_hint: While the server clock is not synchronised, billable sessions are blocked.
time.max_skew_hint: How far the server clock may be off before it counts as not synchronised.
time.trust_os_label: Trust the operating system's clock sync
time.trust_os_hint: Uses the system's own time sync status when the time servers can't be reached, for example behind a firewall.

settings.connection_mode_desc: Whether RustDesk clients connect directly to each other when they can, or always through the relay server.
settings.connection_mode_p2p_first: P2P first (recommended) — try direct connection, fall back to relay
settings.connection_mode_relay_only: Relay only — all sessions use the relay server
settings.connection_mode_same_nat_relay: Force relay when both peers share the same public IP (NAT hairpin)
settings.connection_mode_network_hint: P2P requires UDP port 21116 to be reachable between clients. Signal TCP 21116, relay TCP 21117, NAT test 21115 must be open on the server. Web browser clients always use relay.
settings.connection_mode_not_configurable: Connection mode cannot be changed on this deployment (no systemd unit or docker-compose found)
settings.connection_mode_compose_error: Could not find server environment section in docker-compose.yml
settings.connection_mode_source_defaults: Using server defaults (not writable from panel)
settings.public_endpoints_desc: The addresses RustDesk clients use to reach this server. They appear in the client setup on the overview, in QR codes and in install commands.
settings.public_endpoints_hint: Set these when the web console hostname differs from the RustDesk ID server, relay, or API (reverse proxy / split DNS). Leave empty to auto-detect from the panel URL or Client server address on the Dashboard.
settings.public_endpoints_invalid_host: Invalid ID or relay server hostname
settings.public_endpoints_invalid_api_url: Invalid API URL — use http:// or https:// with a valid host
settings.public_endpoints_env_locked: The server's environment sets this address at every start (PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS_ENV_OVERRIDE=Y), so it can't be changed here. Change it there and restart the server.
settings.public_endpoints_host_extra: Enter only the name or IP address of the server, without http://, a port or a path. Clients use the standard ports.
settings.public_endpoints_host_invalid_ip: This is no valid IPv4 address. Each of its four numbers must be from 0 to 255.
settings.public_endpoints_save_confirm: New client setups, QR codes and install commands will use these addresses.

settings.advanced_select_file: Select a file from the list to view or edit its contents.

settings.advanced_save_confirm: Save changes to this file? A backup of the previous version will be created.
settings.advanced_unsaved_confirm: You have unsaved changes. Discard them?
settings.advanced_no_files: No configuration files available on this system.
settings.advanced_new_file: New file (not created until you save)

settings.advanced_restart_console: The change takes effect after Restart services.

settings.enrollment_desc: How new RustDesk clients are approved on the Join requests page.
settings.enrollment_rich_approve: Full approval form (name, folder, groups, tags)

settings.enrollment_tag_picker: Pick tags from existing device tags

settings.ldap_desc: Configure external authentication via LDAP or Active Directory. Users will be able to sign in with their domain credentials.
settings.ldap_enabled_hint: When enabled, directory users can sign in with LDAP/AD credentials. Each account stays bound to one auth provider (local, LDAP, or OIDC) — local passwords are not accepted for LDAP-bound users.
settings.ldap_timeout_hint: Seconds to wait for the directory, when connecting and for each answer
settings.ldap_direct_bind_hint: Bind directly with a DN template instead of using a service account to search.
settings.ldap_bind_dn_hint: Distinguished Name of a read-only service account used to search for users.
settings.ldap_base_dn_hint: Search base for finding users, e.g. dc=example,dc=com
settings.ldap_user_filter_hint: LDAP filter to find users. Use {{username}} as placeholder. Default: (sAMAccountName={{username}})
settings.ldap_direct_bind_dn_hint: DN template for direct bind. Use {{username}} as placeholder, e.g. uid={{username}},ou=users,dc=example,dc=com
settings.ldap_group_base_dn_hint: Leave empty to use the main Base DN
settings.ldap_group_attr_name_hint: Role map lines can name a group by this attribute, besides its DN or CN. It applies to the groups the group filter finds; groups listed in memberOf are matched by DN or CN.
settings.ldap_allow_signup_hint: A person the directory accepts gets an account at their first sign-in. Off: only people who already have an account can sign in through the directory.
settings.ldap_default_role_hint: Role assigned to users whose LDAP groups don't match any mapping
settings.ldap_group_role_map_hint: Map LDAP groups to NeoDesk roles. Format: GroupDN=role separated by | (pipe). Example: CN=Admins,DC=example,DC=com=admin|CN=Ops,DC=example,DC=com=operator
settings.ldap_test_success: Connection successful! LDAP server is reachable and bind credentials are valid.
settings.oidc_desc: Configure Single Sign-On via an OpenID Connect provider (Azure AD, Okta, Google, Keycloak, etc.).
settings.oidc_enabled_hint: People can sign in with an external identity provider.
settings.oidc_prefer_sso_hint: Automatically start SSO when OIDC is enabled. Use /login?autoLaunch=0 or a private network address for local password login.
settings.oidc_display_name_hint: Text on the sign-in button, for example Azure AD or Okta
settings.oidc_issuer_url_hint: OpenID Connect issuer URL (discovery will be automatic)
settings.oidc_allowed_private_cidrs_hint: Optional comma-separated IPs/CIDRs for an on-premises IdP (for example 10.20.0.0/16). Leave empty to keep private destinations blocked.
settings.oidc_redirect_url_hint: Must match your IdP exactly. Path must be /api/auth/oidc/callback (or /api/oidc/callback). Prefer your panel public URL (this page origin) — the console proxies the callback to the Go API. Direct Go/Client API ports (:21114 / :21121) also work.
settings.oidc_panel_url_hint: URL operators use to open the web console (port 3375 or reverse-proxy hostname). Required for SSO login when the OIDC callback runs on the Go API port.
settings.oidc_group_role_map_hint: One mapping per line: group_name=role (e.g. admins=admin, operators=operator)
settings.oidc_issuer_required: Issuer URL is required to test discovery
settings.device_scope_desc: Controls what non-admin users see when no folder, group, or direct device grants exist.
settings.device_scope_open: Open (legacy) — show all devices until ACL is configured
settings.device_scope_restricted: Restricted — show only explicitly granted devices
settings.device_scope_restricted_warning: Restricted mode is active. Ensure users have folder, group, or direct device grants or they will see an empty device list.
settings.availability_history_desc: Optionally record when devices change online/offline status so Metrics can show a day-by-day history. Disabled by default to avoid database growth.
settings.availability_history_enable_hint: When enabled, the Go server records status transitions (ONLINE, OFFLINE, DEGRADED, CRITICAL) observed from heartbeats and signal/CDAP/Mesh activity.
settings.availability_history_retention_hint: Older events are deleted automatically. Default is 30 days.
settings.backend_desc: Choose which server backend to use for device management and signal/relay services.
settings.backend_rustdesk_desc: Standard RustDesk signal and relay servers (hbbs + hbbr). Basic HTTP API with limited endpoints.
settings.backend_neodesk_desc: Enhanced Go-based server with full REST API, JWT authentication, blocklist, tags, real-time WebSocket events, and audit logging.
settings.backend_saved: Server backend changed successfully. Device data will now be managed by the new backend.
settings.backend_confirm_switch: Are you sure you want to switch the server backend? This will change how devices are managed.
settings.backend_unreachable: Cannot switch: target server is unreachable. Start the server first.
settings.totp_desc: Add an extra layer of security with TOTP authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, Authy, etc.)
settings.totp_enabled_desc: Your account is protected with two-factor sign-in.
settings.totp_disabled_desc: Turn on two-factor sign-in to protect your account better.
settings.totp_step1: Install an authenticator app on your phone
settings.totp_recovery_warning: Save these recovery codes in a safe place. Each code can only be used once. If you lose access to your authenticator app, you can use these codes to log in.
settings.totp_disable_warning: Disabling two-factor authentication will make your account less secure.
settings.go_server_version_dev_hint: Go binary reports development build — rebuild or update the server to match the product version

email.err_identity_email: Enter one address, such as it@example.com.

email.preview_kind_impersonation: Admin viewed the console as someone

Opt-in. When several live peers share one public IP and the client has no login token or udp_port, authorize as shared-nat-initiator. Does not inherit another device identity. Weakens managed enrollment outbound gate for that NAT — enable only for CGNAT/office sites that cannot use account login.

settings.connection_mode_operator_only_outbound_h: Opt-in. Stock RustDesk clients must use an active NeoDesk session with device.connect permission to start PunchHole or relay connections. Approved endpoints without that login cannot initiate; Web Remote remains available through panel authentication.

general.endpoint_id_hint: Host name or IP address of the ID server, as clients on the internet reach it.
general.endpoint_relay_hint: Leave empty to use the ID server address.
general.endpoints_effect: Applies right away to the client setup values, QR codes and install commands. Devices already set up keep their old address until they are set up again.
general.conn_fallback_hint: How long a client tries a direct connection before it uses the relay.
general.conn_fallback_error: Enter a whole number of milliseconds from 0 to 30000.
general.conn_effect: Applies to new connections. If the server cannot apply it directly, you are asked to restart the server after saving.
general.conn_running: The server runs with: {mode}, direct attempt {ms} ms.
general.scope_open_desc: People see every device except those in folders and groups with an access list, which only the people on the list see.
general.scope_restricted_desc: People see only the devices they were given access to.
general.scope_effect: Applies right away to everyone who is not an administrator.
general.availability_effect: Applies right away. Turning it off stops recording; events already recorded stay until they expire.
general.mesh_note: Lets MeshCentral agents connect to this server. Download a .msh file to install the agent on a device.
general.mesh_groups_effect: Applies right away to agents that connect after saving.
general.mesh_group_needs_both: Enter a group ID and a display name.
general.audit_moved: The console activity log is under
general.endpoint_api_hint: Full address clients use to sign in, for example https://api.example.com. The server uses port 21121 unless you changed it.
general.endpoints_when: Fill these in when clients reach this server under another address than this console, for example behind a reverse proxy. Empty fields use the address found automatically, shown under What clients get now.
general.conn_p2p_desc: Computers connect directly when their networks allow it, otherwise through the relay server.
general.conn_relay_desc: Every session goes through the relay server.
general.conn_same_nat: Use the relay when both computers have the same public IP address
general.conn_same_nat_hint: Some routers can't pass a direct connection between two computers behind the same public address.
general.conn_shared_nat: Let devices that share a public IP address start sessions without signing in
general.conn_shared_nat_hint: Off by default. Turn it on only for sites where many devices share one public IP address and can't sign in to an account. It weakens the check on who may start a session from that address.
general.conn_logged_in: Only signed-in RustDesk apps can start sessions
general.conn_logged_in_hint: The RustDesk app must be signed in to a NeoDesk account to start a session. Sessions from the browser are not affected. The remote device still asks for its password or approval.
general.conn_operator_only: Only accounts that may connect to devices can start sessions
general.conn_operator_only_hint: The RustDesk app must be signed in to an account that may connect to devices. Other devices can't start sessions. Sessions from the browser still work.
general.conn_ports_hint: Direct connections need UDP port 21116 open between the two computers. On the server, TCP ports 21115 to 21117 and UDP port 21116 must be open. Sessions in the browser always use the relay.
general.conn_readonly: This console can't change the connection strategy on this server, because it found no service settings to save it in. The server uses the choice shown here. To change it, set it where the server is started (docker-compose.yml or its systemd service).
general.conn_readonly_short: This console can't change the connection strategy on this server.
general.scope_note: What people who are not administrators see before you give them access to folders, groups or devices.
general.scope_restricted_warning: People who have no access to any folder, group or device will see an empty device list.
general.availability_note: Records when devices go online or offline, so Metrics can show a history by day. Off by default, because it makes the database grow.
general.availability_enable_hint: The server notes every change of a device's status, for example from online to offline.
general.retention_hint: Older entries are deleted automatically. Default: 30 days.
general.retention_error: Enter a whole number of days from 1 to 3650.
general.mesh_note2: Devices with MeshAgent, the agent of MeshCentral, can connect to this server too.
general.mesh_off: MeshCentral is turned off on this server, so MeshAgent devices can't connect. It is on unless the server is started with MESH_ENABLED=N.
general.mesh_cert_missing: The agent certificate was not found. Once agents have connected, back up the file mesh_agent_server.pem.
general.mesh_groups_note: Each group has its own .msh file. Devices installed with a group's file join that group.
general.mesh_groups_empty: No mesh groups yet. Add one to get a .msh file for it.
general.mesh_group_remove_msg: Remove "{name}"? New .msh files can no longer use this group.
general.mesh_group_name_hint: The name people see for this group.

general.mesh_group_id_invalid: Use letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores, without spaces.
general.mesh_group_exists: A group with this ID already exists.

signin.ldap_effect: Applies to the next sign-in. People already signed in stay signed in.
signin.oidc_effect: Applies to the next sign-in. People already signed in stay signed in.
signin.totp_note: Each time you sign in, you also enter a code from an app on your phone, such as Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or Authy.
signin.require_2fa_hint: A local account without two-factor sign-in sets it up right after its next password sign-in and can do nothing else until then; the desktop client and the API refuse it until it has. Directory and single sign-on accounts are left to their provider.
signin.ldap_enabled_hint: People from your directory sign in with their directory user name and password. Each account uses one way to sign in, so directory accounts can't use a password set in this console.

signin.single_session_hint: A new sign-in signs out the account's other browser. Off: an account can be signed in on up to {max} browsers and devices at once.
signin.oidc_advanced_note: Needed only when the provider has no discovery document, or sits in a private network.
signin.impersonation_mail: Mail people when an admin views NeoDesk as them
signin.impersonation_mail_hint: The mail says who looked, when and why. Accounts without an email address get none; everyone sees it in their recent sign-ins.
signin.client_sessions_next: Applies from the next sign-in of a RustDesk app. Apps signed in now keep their session.
signin.expiry_help: When Extend session on activity is off, apps must sign in again after this many days.
signin.max_days_help: Upper limit for the renewal, counted from the first sign-in.
signin.max_days_off: Has no effect while Extend session on activity is off.
signin.console_note: Rules for every account that signs in to this console.
signin.console_effect: Applies from the next sign-in. People signed in now stay signed in.
signin.single_session_on: A new sign-in signs out the account's other browser.
signin.sessions_any: An account can be signed in on any number of browsers and devices at once.
signin.sessions_up_to: An account can be signed in on up to {max} browsers and devices at once.

backup_tab.create_note: One .tar.gz file with the console data, server keys, environment file, uploaded images and the server database. You can restore it on this or a new server.
backup_tab.super_admin_only: Only a super admin can download, schedule or restore full backups, because a backup holds every secret of the server.
backup_tab.retention_hint: Older backups are deleted after each new one.
backup_tab.retention_error: Enter a whole number of backups from 1 to 365.
backup_tab.schedule_effect: Applies right away. The next backup runs on the new schedule.
backup_tab.smb_effect: Saving stores the login details only. The share must be mounted on the server to be used as a destination.
backup_tab.restore_note: Restoring replaces data on this server with the data in the backup. Make a backup first.
backup_tab.restore_file_hint: A .tar.gz file made on this page, or an older .json settings file.
backup_tab.restore_nothing: Nothing was restored. The backup holds none of the parts you chose.
backup_tab.restore_partial: Not everything was restored. The list below shows what was restored and what was skipped.
backup_tab.not_archive: This file is no backup archive. Choose a .tar.gz file made on this page.
backup_tab.opt_database_desc: Accounts, settings, folders, groups and everything else the web console stores, but not what Server device database holds. Replaces what is there now. Applies right away.
backup_tab.opt_uploads_desc: Logos and background pictures uploaded under Appearance. Files with the same name are replaced.
backup_tab.opt_secrets_desc: Replaces the server key, the API key and the session secret. Everyone is signed out. If the backup comes from another server, every client must be set up again. Needs a service restart.
backup_tab.opt_env_desc: Replaces the console's ports, database connection, API key and session secret. Needs a service restart.
backup_tab.opt_godb_desc: Registered devices, device tokens, organizations, billing, chat, RDP and VNC targets, changed role permissions and the server's own settings. Accounts and the rest of the console data stay as they are. Needs a service restart.
backup_tab.restore_json_note: This is an older settings file. It restores console settings, appearance, device folders, groups and address books. The choices above do not apply to it.
backup_tab.confirm_intro: These are replaced with the contents of {file}:
backup_tab.schedule_note: Makes a full backup on the server at set times and checks that it can be read back. Older copies are deleted once there are more than you keep.
backup_tab.schedule_enabled_hint: When this is on, you choose how often, how many copies to keep and where they are saved.
backup_tab.smb_note: Only needed when backups go to a Windows share or a NAS. Save the login here and test it. The share must also be mounted on the server, at the folder you choose as the destination.
backup_tab.smb_domain_hint: Leave empty unless the share belongs to a Windows domain.
backup_tab.smb_mount_path: Folder where the share is mounted
backup_tab.smb_mount_path_hint: The same folder you enter as the destination of scheduled backups.
backup_tab.restore_start: Choose a backup file. Then you pick what to restore from it.
backup_tab.restore_pick_parts: Tick at least one part to restore.
backup_tab.contents_note: What a backup made now would contain.
backup_tab.create_note_parts: One .tar.gz file with {parts}. You can restore it on this or a new server.
backup_tab.create_note_plain: One .tar.gz file you can restore on this or a new server.
backup_tab.warning_parts: This backup contains secrets: {parts}. Store it securely and never share it.
backup_tab.warning_plain: This backup contains secrets. Store it securely and never share it.
backup_tab.reason_docker: Docker installs take their settings from the container, there is no environment file to save.
backup_tab.reason_environment: Set by SESSION_SECRET in the environment, there is no file to save.
backup_tab.reason_postgres: The database is PostgreSQL: its data is in the backup, there is no database file.
backup_tab.reason_not_configured: Not set up on this server.
backup_tab.reason_no_server: The console can't reach the server.

updates_tab.desc: See whether a newer NeoDesk version is out, and install it.
updates_tab.docker_desc: This server runs from ready-made Docker images. To update it, run these commands on the host. Installing from this page is turned off.
updates_tab.docker_install_note: Run the commands above on the host, then reload this page.
updates_tab.channel_note: Which versions this server is offered.
updates_tab.channel_stable_desc: Tested releases. Use this on servers people depend on.
updates_tab.channel_development_desc: The newest changes before they are released. Things can break.
updates_tab.channel_effect: Saved as soon as you confirm. Check for updates again afterwards.
updates_tab.channel_docker_note: With Docker the image tag decides the channel: set NEODESK_IMAGE_TAG to latest for Stable or dev for Development, then run the update commands.
updates_tab.channel_confirm: Switch updates to {to}? The next check compares your version with the {to} channel.
updates_tab.backups_note: Before each update the console saves the files it replaces. You can put them back from here.
updates_tab.idle_note: Checking asks GitHub for the newest version. Nothing is installed until you click Install.
updates_tab.channel_applies: Applies to the next check for updates. Nothing is installed until you click Install.
updates_tab.channel_applies_short: Applies to the next check for updates.

advanced_tab.restart_row: Restart the service of this file
advanced_tab.restart_desc: Saved changes to this file take effect after a restart. Open sessions drop for a moment.
advanced_tab.status_new: Not created yet. Saving creates it.
advanced_tab.status_readonly: Read only. The console can show it but not change it.
advanced_tab.missing_note: These files don't exist on this server, so they can't be edited here.

side.general_note: The addresses RustDesk clients get from this server right now: in the client setup, QR codes and install commands.
side.local_warning: These addresses only work on this computer. Other computers and phones can't reach them. Enter the server's address under Public client endpoints.
side.preview_note: The console with the choices on this page. Save to apply them.
side.preview_note_all: The console with the choices on this page. After you save, everyone sees them the next time they load a page.

restart_prompt.message_progress: The NeoDesk services are restarting. Keep this page open.

settings.inactive_label: Disable accounts that don't sign in
settings.inactive_hint: An account that hasn't signed in for the number of days below is disabled. The person gets an email {notice} days before. Accounts kept in Edit user, open invites, pro accounts and the last Super admin are left alone.
settings.inactive_days_invalid: Enter a whole number of days from {min} to {max}.

notices.title: Security notices
notices.note: Mails to people about their own account, in their language. They go out only when email is set up and the account has an address.
notices.new_signin_hint: When an account signs in from a browser it hasn't used before. The console sets a cookie to recognise the browser.
notices.password_changed_hint: Changed by the person, with a reset link, or by an admin.
notices.two_factor_changed_hint: Turned on, turned off or reset, and recovery codes used up, renewed or made unusable.

brand.name_help: Shown in the sidebar, the browser tab and on the sign-in page. Empty uses NeoDesk.
brand.footer_help: For example a copyright notice or your company name. Empty shows no text.
brand.login_title_help: The big line on the sign-in page. Empty shows "{text}".
brand.login_subtitle_help: A line under the heading. Empty shows none.
brand.slide_upload_help: Uploaded when you pick it and used once you save.
brand.slide_url_help: Filled in when you upload a picture. An address on this server, for example /img/login-slides/free.jpg.
brand.login_bg_help: What shows behind the sign-in form.
brand.agent_bg_help: What shows behind the download page.
brand.rdclient_bg_help: What shows behind the device list. "{inherit}" uses the console background.
brand.website_help: A full address, for example https://example.com.

joining.mode_note: Which new devices may join this server, and how.
joining.mode_effect: Applies to the next device that asks to join. Devices that already joined stay.
joining.approve_open: Applies only to Mesh agents while the join mode is Open: RustDesk clients join without approval.
joining.tags_needs_form: Has no effect while the full approval form is off: Approve then asks for no tags.
joining.scope_help: Administrators always see every device. Access to folders, groups and devices is given on their pages.
joining.retention_off: Has no effect while availability history is off.

ldap.only_direct: Used only while Direct bind is on.
ldap.not_direct: Not used while Direct bind is on.
ldap.off_note: These settings do nothing while LDAP sign-in is off. You can fill them in and test the connection first.
ldap.signin_note: People sign in to the console with their account from your directory, such as Active Directory.
ldap.connection_note: Where the console reaches your directory server.
ldap.host_help: Host name or IP address of the directory server, without ldap:// and without a port. For example ldap.example.com.
ldap.port_help: Usually 389, or 636 with LDAPS. Empty: the usual port.
ldap.tls_help: Connect with TLS from the start, usually on port 636. Turning it on or off moves the port along.
ldap.start_tls_help: Start without TLS on the usual port and switch to TLS before signing in.
ldap.skip_verify_help: Accepts any certificate from the directory. Use it only to test with a self-signed certificate.
ldap.timeout_help: Seconds to wait for the directory, when connecting and for each answer. Empty: 10 seconds.
ldap.bind_note: Either a service account searches for the person, or the console signs in with a name built from what they typed.
ldap.direct_bind_help: Sign in with a DN built from the name the person types, without a service account.
ldap.bind_dn_help: A read-only account that searches for people. For example cn=readonly,dc=example,dc=com.
ldap.bind_password_help: The password of the service account.
ldap.base_dn_help: Where people are searched. For example dc=example,dc=com.
ldap.user_filter_help: How a person is found by the name they type, with {{username}} where the name goes. Empty: (sAMAccountName={{username}}). For example (uid={{username}}).
ldap.direct_bind_dn_help: The DN to sign in with, with {{username}} where the name goes. For example uid={{username}},ou=users,dc=example,dc=com.
ldap.attr_id_help: The attribute with the sign-in name. For example sAMAccountName or uid.
ldap.groups_note: Which role people get, from the groups they are in.
ldap.groups_effect: A person gets the role at each sign-in through the directory.
ldap.group_base_dn_help: Where groups are searched. Empty: the Base DN. For example ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com.
ldap.group_filter_help: How a person's groups are found, with {{dn}} for the person's DN. For example (member={{dn}}).
ldap.group_attr_help: Role map entries can name a group by this attribute, besides its DN or CN. For example cn.
ldap.default_role_help: The role of people whose groups match no entry of the map below.
ldap.role_map_help: One entry per group: the group by its DN or name, and the role its people get. For example CN=NeoDesk Admins,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=com with Administrator.
ldap.off_note_page: LDAP sign-in is off, so the settings on this page do nothing yet. You can fill them in and test the connection first.

sso.manual_unused: Used only while Auto-discovery is off, or when the provider has no discovery document.
sso.off_note: These settings do nothing while single sign-on is off. You can fill them in and test discovery first.
sso.signin_note: People sign in to the console with an account from an identity provider such as Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Google or Keycloak (OpenID Connect).
sso.enabled_help: The sign-in page gets a button for the provider. Turning it on fills in the redirect URL and the console address when they are empty.
sso.provider_note: What the provider gave you when you registered the console with it.
sso.display_name_help: The text on the sign-in button. For example Microsoft or Okta.
sso.issuer_help: The provider address that hands out its settings. For example https://login.microsoftonline.com/your-tenant/v2.0.
sso.client_id_help: The ID the provider gave the console.
sso.client_secret_help: The secret the provider gave the console.
sso.redirect_help: Where the provider sends people back. Enter the same address at the provider. It ends in /api/auth/oidc/callback, for example {url}.
sso.panel_help: The address people open the console at, after a reverse proxy if there is one. For example {url}.
sso.scopes_help: What the console asks the provider for, separated by spaces. Usually openid profile email.
sso.pkce_help: Protects the sign-in against a stolen code. Turn it off only if the provider refuses it.
sso.discovery_help: The console reads the endpoints from the issuer. Off: enter them below.
sso.cidrs_help: For a provider on your own network: one address or range per row. For example 10.20.0.0/16 or 192.168.50.10. Empty: the console reaches no private address.
sso.accounts_note: Who gets an account and how the sign-in page starts.
sso.signup_help: A person the provider accepts gets an account at their first sign-in. Off: only people who already have an account can sign in this way.
sso.prefer_help: The sign-in page goes to the provider at once. To sign in with a password instead, open /login?autoLaunch=0.
sso.claim_groups_help: The claim with the groups for the role map below. For example groups.
sso.roles_note: Which role people get, from their groups at the provider.
sso.roles_effect: A person gets the role at each sign-in through the provider.
sso.default_role_help: The role of people whose groups match no entry of the map below.
sso.role_map_help: One entry per group: the group as the provider names it, and the role its people get. For example neodesk-admins with Administrator.
sso.off_note_page: Single sign-on is off, so the settings on this page do nothing yet. You can fill them in and test discovery first.

mesh.groups_effect: Adding, renaming and removing a group saves at once. Devices already installed stay in their group.
mesh.install_note: Download the .msh file of a group and install MeshAgent with it on the device.
mesh.msh_name_help: MeshAgent shows this name for the server. It only goes into the downloaded file and is not saved. The file is for the group with the ID default; for another group, use the menu in its row.
mesh.msh_name_help_short: MeshAgent shows this name for the server. It only goes into the downloaded file and is not saved.
mesh.install_group_help: Devices installed with the file join this group.

cross_platform.limit_mac_signing: To hand the agent out to Macs, it has to be signed with an Apple Developer ID.
cross_platform.limit_mac_notarize: Outside the App Store, macOS only opens the agent after Apple has checked it (notarization).
cross_platform.limit_android_projection: The person on the device has to agree each time the screen is shared.

cross_platform.limit_ios_capture: iOS doesn't allow screen capture in the background. Only viewing is supported.

cross_platform.limit_chrome_pwa: As a web app, only the browser features are available, not the agent's.

device_offline.why: It has not checked in with the server for a while.
device_offline.todo: Turn it on or wake it up, and check that NeoDesk runs on it. Then reconnect.

device_unknown.why: No computer with this ID is registered on this server.
device_unknown.todo: Check the ID. If the computer was removed, add it again under Add computers.

device_revoked.why: Someone revoked this computer in the console, so the server refuses it, even when it is on.
device_revoked.todo: If it should connect again, unblock it here. Then reconnect.
device_revoked.todo_ask: Ask an administrator to unblock this computer, then reconnect.

device_blocked.why: Its ID is on the server's blocklist, so the server refuses it, even when it is on.
device_blocked.todo: If it should connect again, unblock it here. Then reconnect.
device_blocked.todo_ask: Ask an administrator to unblock this computer, then reconnect.

device_banned.why: An administrator banned this computer, so the server refuses it.
device_banned.todo: If it should connect again, unban it in the device panel.

device_removed.why: The computer is with the deleted devices.
device_removed.todo: Restore it in the device panel, or add it again under Add computers.

device_rejected.why: An administrator rejected this computer when it asked to join.
device_rejected.todo: Ask an administrator to allow it under Add computers, then try again.

other_machine.what: Another computer already uses the ID of {name}.
other_machine.why: The server knows this ID from a different machine.
other_machine.todo: Ask an administrator to delete the old device in the console, then try again.

key_changed.what: {name} came back with a new key.
key_changed.why: The server refuses a computer whose key changed until an administrator approves it. This keeps others from taking over its ID.
key_changed.todo: If you expected the change, approve the new key in the device panel. Then reconnect.

join_proof.what: {name} could not prove that it is the computer the server knows.
join_proof.why: The ID is enrolled already, and this computer did not sign the join with the key the server has for it.
join_proof.todo: Update NeoDesk on this computer and open the link again, or ask an administrator to delete the old device in the console.

server_unreachable.what: This browser can't reach the NeoDesk server.
server_unreachable.why: The server did not answer when the connection started.
server_unreachable.todo: Check your network, then reconnect. If it keeps failing, ask an administrator to check the server.

relay_unreachable.what: The connection to {name} could not be set up.
relay_unreachable.why: This browser could not reach the part of the server that carries the session.
relay_unreachable.todo: Reconnect. If it keeps failing, ask an administrator to check that the server's ports are open.

relay_refused.what: The server stopped the connection to {name}.
relay_refused.why: The server did not let this session through.
relay_refused.todo: Reconnect. If it keeps happening, copy the details and send them to an administrator.

no_answer.why: The server asked {name} to connect, and no answer came in time. It may be asleep or busy, or its network may block NeoDesk.
no_answer.todo: Wake it up or wait a moment, then reconnect.

not_authorized.why: The server does not let your account start sessions to this computer.
not_authorized.todo: Ask an administrator to give you access to this computer.

feature_off.what: This kind of session is turned off for your account.
feature_off.why: An administrator turned it off in your account's client features.
feature_off.todo: Ask an administrator to turn it on.

consent_scope.why: In this quick support session, {person} allowed only some things.
consent_scope.todo: Ask {person} to allow it in the quick support window.

license_blocked.what: The server's license does not allow this connection.
license_blocked.why: The license key does not match this server.
license_blocked.todo: Ask an administrator to check the license.

session_limit.what: The server takes no more sessions right now.
session_limit.why: The number of sessions is at the limit of its license.
session_limit.todo: Wait until another session ends, or ask an administrator.

billing_blocked.what: The server does not allow sessions to {name} right now.
billing_blocked.why: The contract of this computer does not allow sessions.
billing_blocked.todo: Ask an administrator to check the computer's contract.

client_too_old.what: NeoDesk on {name} is too old for this.
client_too_old.why: The version on the computer does not support this connection.

consent_declined.why: The person at {name} clicked Decline or closed the window that asked.
consent_declined.todo: Ask them to try again, then reconnect.

consent_timeout.why: Nobody accepted the connection on {name} within 3 minutes.
consent_timeout.todo: Ask them to watch for the window that asks, then reconnect.

consent_not_allowed.what: {person} has not allowed quick support yet.
consent_not_allowed.why: {name} offers to let you in by click only after the person clicked Allow in the quick support window.
consent_not_allowed.todo: Ask them to click Allow in the quick support window, then connect again.

consent_needs_https.what: {name} can't let you in by click.
consent_needs_https.why: This console is not on HTTPS, so quick support takes only the one-time password.
consent_needs_https.todo: Send a new quick support link: its one-time password comes to you and connects you. To accept by click, the console needs HTTPS.

consent_needs_update.what: {name} can't let you in by click.
consent_needs_update.why: NeoDesk on {name} is too old to accept by click.
consent_needs_update.todo: Send a new quick support link: its one-time password comes to you and connects you. Or ask {person} to update NeoDesk.

password_wrong.todo: Enter the password set on {name}. NeoDesk shows it on that computer under Settings, Security.

tfa_wrong.todo: Enter the current code from the authenticator app linked to {name}.

rate_limited.why: {name} blocks sign-ins for a while after several wrong ones.

device_not_allowed.why: NeoDesk on {name} only lets people in with a password, and no password is set there, or its settings turn connections off.
device_not_allowed.todo: Ask someone at {name} to set a password or allow connections under Settings, Security.

device_blocks_you.why: NeoDesk on {name} has your ID or address on its own blocklist.
device_blocks_you.todo: Ask someone at {name} to remove the block in its settings.

device_feature_off.why: NeoDesk on {name} does not allow this kind of session.
device_feature_off.todo: Ask someone at {name} to allow it under Settings, Security.

device_not_installed.what: {name} can't do this without an installed NeoDesk.
device_not_installed.why: NeoDesk runs there without being installed, and this needs the installed version.
device_not_installed.todo: Ask someone at {name} to install NeoDesk, then reconnect.

login_screen.what: {name} shows a sign-in screen NeoDesk can't share.
login_screen.why: The sign-in screen of {name} runs on Wayland, which NeoDesk can't capture.
login_screen.todo: Sign in on {name} first, or switch its sign-in screen to X11. Then reconnect.

privacy_mode.what: Someone turned on privacy mode on {name}.
privacy_mode.why: Another session holds {name} in privacy mode, which lets no second viewer in.
privacy_mode.todo: Wait until that session ends, then reconnect.

device_not_ready.what: {name} is not ready for this connection.
device_not_ready.why: NeoDesk on {name} said it can't take the session now.
device_not_ready.todo: Ask someone at {name} to open NeoDesk, then reconnect.

insecure.what: The connection to {name} was stopped because it could not be secured.
insecure.why: {name} did not prove its identity or did not encrypt the connection. Someone between this browser and the computer may be listening in, or the server key is not set up.
insecure.todo: No password was sent. Ask an administrator to check the server.

https_required.what: {name} can't be shown over plain HTTP.
https_required.why: This computer sends a video format the browser plays only over HTTPS.
https_required.todo: Open the console over HTTPS to see its screen.

signin_closed.what: {name} closed the connection when this browser signed in.
signin_closed.todo: Reconnect and sign in again. If it keeps happening, ask an administrator to look at the log of NeoDesk on the computer.

dropped_early.why: The network between this browser, the server and {name} was interrupted while the session started.
dropped_early.todo: Reconnect. If it keeps happening, check the network of the computer.

dropped.why: The network between this browser, the server and {name} was interrupted.
dropped.todo: Reconnect. If it keeps happening, check the network of the computer.

unknown.why: The cause is not known. The details below show what this browser saw.
unknown.todo: Reconnect. If it keeps failing, copy the details and send them to an administrator.

security.not_you_two_factor: If you didn't expect this, change your password and tell your administrator right away.
security.not_you_email: If you didn't expect this, tell your administrator right away.
